settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: JsonPatchHandler.apply asserts request.isPatchRequest() and the controller only routes JSON Patch/merge-patch media types (ACCEPT_PATCH_HEADERS), limiting the entry point to PATCH operations.
JsonPatchPatchConverter.convert rejects non-ArrayNode bodies and unknown op types (throws PatchException), and valueFromJsonNode only accepts scalar/object/array nodes, so the op type is constrained.

PatchOperation wraps SpelEvaluationException and ExpressionException into PatchException, and JsonPatchHandler wraps conversion failures into HttpMessageNotReadableException, so malformed input fails fast rather than executing after an error.

Spring Expression Language's reflective/T() style access is gated by the SpelParserConfiguration / EvaluationContext used by the embedding application, not by code in this file; those settings are outside the inspected source.
candidates.description: JsonPatchHandler.applyPatch builds a Patch from the request body via JsonPatchPatchConverter.convert(), which extracts the attacker-controlled "path" (and "from") strings for each operation and constructs PatchOperation subclasses. PatchOperation's constructor calls PathToSpEL.pathToExpression(path), which joins the '/'-separated nodes and calls SpelExpressionParser.parseExpression(...). The resulting Expression is then evaluated/set against the target entity in PatchOperation.getValueFromTarget/setValueOnTarget/popValueAtPath and in addValue via pathToParentExpression. PathToSpEL does the reverse conversion only in a naive way: nodes are appended verbatim unless they parse as an integer (then emitted as [index]) or are the '-' append token (then emitted as $[true]); at line 106-112 an empty result becomes"#this". There is no validation/allow-list that a path segment corresponds to an actual persistent property, so arbitrary SpEL text contained in a path segment (e.g. method invocations, property chains, type references) is passed to the parser. Because the expression is evaluated with a user-controlled domain object as root, this is a candidate for expression injection / unintended property or method access via PATCH request paths. Root cause: trust boundary between request payload (path/from) and SpEL expression construction, with no sanitization or restriction to property/projection names.
missing_evidence: The SpelParserConfiguration (e.g. addCompilerMode/restrict reflective access) and EvaluationContext/root object wiring used by the hosting application were not found in the read-only source.
No test or configuration in this repository demonstrates whether crafted path segments such as a method invocation actually reach the parser and evaluate, versus being rejected by SpEL grammar.
The resolved Spring Framework version (parent is spring-data-parent 2.0.0.BUILD-SNAPSHOT, not pinned here) determines the available SpEL restrictions and whether type references are reachable.
We did not trace all callers of pathToExpression/pathToParentExpression to prove a fully attacker-reachable chain from the HTTP layer to evaluation.
preconditions: Application exposes the Spring Data REST PATCH endpoint (JSON Patch media type application/json-patch+json) for a repository resource.
An attacker can submit a PATCH request body containing a JSON Patch array with a crafted "path" (or "from") value.
The expression is evaluated against an entity whose class exposes properties/methods the attacker wishes to reach.
The SpEL parser/evaluation context in use does not itself block the crafted construct (parser configuration not present in this repository).
candidates.title: Client-supplied JSON Patch path/from values are compiled into SpEL expressions and evaluated against domain objects
